rationale: Reviewed a593792a5795a19639deba83bff6970566d91032, the complete current BRIEF, my round-3 verdict, consolidated-round-3.md, the resulting spec and ADR-0045, and relevant production code. My sole round-3 ask is ADDRESSED. All six requested baseline claims were reproduced with fresh scratch-only probes. Two new specification gaps remain: an old genuine reattest audit can survive a normal executor binding replacement and satisfy the stated fallback read-back predicate for an unvouched pair; and the N4 positional override promise includes beads with no lineage, which fail before MF-1 can be evaluated. These require specification and AC corrections before planning, not delivery of the future implementation at the spec gate. Spec validation exits 0 with one lifecycle-binding warning. GitHub API access was unavailable. The source worktree was treated read-only; the clone, fake bd scripts, real git fixtures, embedded bd database, build cache and probe logs are all under the assigned scratch directory.
concrete_changes_required: Bind fallback read-back authority to the exact pair accepted by reattest, rather than the presence of audit keys plus a matching scanned-branch string (R4.2, spec.md:374-378). Define machine-readable audited AFTER merge SHA and second parent, or an equivalently unambiguous checked identity, and require it to equal both the current binding and the candidate. An executor replacement must not inherit authority from an audit for a different pair. Add an AC-11 regression that obtains a genuine audit for M1, uses the existing executor binding writer to replace the binding with M2 while preserving old metadata, moves the landings off first-parent, and verifies automatic refusal: M2 has never been reattested and a fresh fallback reattest refuses the two candidates. This can be implemented by extending the reattest audit and its reader without expanding the executor-change non-goal; it does not require authenticating metadata or rejecting the explicitly accepted deliberate-forgery residual.

Restrict N4's MF-1-only positional override promise to beads whose lineage resolves to E. R1.2 N4 explicitly includes lineage-none beads (spec.md:266), but R1.3:280 says every N4 positional reaches an MF-1 NOT-READY report and can then be deliberately claimed by overriding MF-1. Specify the lineage-none N4 refusal and truthful diagnostic separately; it needs lineage repair before any readiness override can help, or work outside next. Preserve the no-automatic-selection and informational classification if desired. Add an AC covering an unmapped <E>.N bead with no parent/dependency and a neutral title, asserting that the scoped MF-1 override cannot bypass lineage resolution and that no mutation occurs.

findings.title: Round-3 ask status
findings.detail: G1r3.1 ADDRESSED. R6.4 now emits --allow-not-ready=<all currently failing ids>, explicitly distinguishes the uncovered diagnostic from fresh claim scope, and reiterates replacement rather than union. AC-17 now pins MF-2-covered/MF-3-uncovered, a successful release plus fresh MF-2,MF-3 re-claim, the narrower MF-3-only refusal, the MF-3/MF-4 analogue, and coverage lost through digest growth. The scratch policy probe logs uncovered=[MF-3], fresh requested=[MF-2 MF-3], matching the revised set contract. The two findings below are NEW_ISSUEs in the round-4 design, not reopened round-3 asks. Evidence: probes.log and repo/internal/validate/readiness/g1_round4_probe_test.go.

findings.title: A genuine old reattest audit can authorize a different executor-written binding
findings.detail: R4.2:374-378 makes read-back an iff of (1) the current binding matching the candidate pair and (2) reattest audit metadata with this scanned branch. Production ReattestLandedMerge writes actor/at/op/corroboration/prior-pair/scanned-branch keys, but no structured audited-after pair. Production MindspecExecutor.ensureLandedBinding replaces only mindspec_landed_merge_sha, mindspec_landed_second_parent and mindspec_landed_at through bead.MergeMetadata, which preserves every old audit key. TestG1R4StaleReattestAudit uses a real git repo, a fake bd on PATH, the real ReattestLandedMerge, the real ensureLandedBinding and the real MergeMetadata. It obtains an audit for M1, makes a second landing M2 of the same bead, and lets the executor write M2's binding. All seven audit keys remain byte-identical and still describe M1. After the #239 topology, both M1 and M2 are admitted reachable off-first-parent candidates, and the current binding exactly matches M2. The two stated read-back conditions are true even though M2 was never operator-vouched and a fresh fallback reattest would refuse Ambiguous. This is routine stale-metadata inheritance, not the explicitly accepted deliberate metadata forge. Production metadata behavior is exercised directly; acceptance by the not-yet-built fallback is a labeled emulation of the normative predicate. Evidence: probes.log; repo/internal/executor/g1_round4_probe_test.go; production internal/executor/mindspec_executor.go:1771, internal/bead/bdcli.go:322, internal/lifecycle/reattest.go:363.

findings.title: N4 promises an MF-1 override for beads that cannot reach MF-1
findings.detail: N4 includes plan-form IDs with lineage E OR NONE (spec.md:266), and R1.3:280 universally says an N4 positional is refused NOT-READY on MF-1 and can be claimed with the scoped MF-1 override. For an unmapped probe-epic.7 with no parent/dependency and neutral title, the real phase resolver returns ErrNoEpicLineage. The real GateReadiness(root,id,true), even with today's broader all-signal override, returns report=nil and 'evaluating readiness ... resolving owning spec ... no epic lineage'. MF-1 was never evaluated. R1.8 expressly preserves that pre-signal refusal, so the new N4 promise conflicts with both the unchanged resolver and its own spec contract. The usual parented N4 case is sound; narrow the promise and test the detached case. Evidence: probes.log and repo/internal/next/g1_round4_probe_test.go.

findings.title: Six baseline claims reproduced at the reviewed commit
findings.detail: Fake bd on PATH: a globally ready probe-epic.1 disappears under an edge-only --parent query; BuildReadySet returns raw=0/filtered=0 and an empty notice. A successful 'Showing 100 of 106 ready issues' stderr notice is discarded; QueryReady returns 100 rows with nil error. Real git: the first-parent control identifies the landing, the same merge remains reachable after sibling integration but FindLandedMerge returns ErrLandedMergeNoCandidate. Two real panel.json registrations sorted a-stale then z-match produce a stale-SHA contradiction despite a correct surviving tip; removing the stale registration restores the control. MF-2: R9(a) against identical spec text reports dangling; AC9 harvests zero claims. Real bd 1.1.0 (8e4e59d39), in a new embedded scratch database: ready --metadata-field spec_id=129-probe -n 0 returns both the detached dotted child and the metadata-only task; ready --parent still returns the detached child by prefix; ready -n 1 returns one of four rows and emits its cap notice at exit 0. This supports the corrected Background A: the fake parent-drop demonstrates edge-only behavior, not bd 1.1.0's prefix behavior. Evidence: probes.log, bd-real-probes.json, bd-ids.json and the four g1_round4_probe_test.go files in the scratch clone. The historical live-tracker count of 106 was not re-measured.

findings.title: MF-1 mapping probe and accepted audit trust boundary
findings.detail: The actual extractBeadSectionRaw mapping is positional: a file with only a heading '## Bead 7' maps that section to index 1, not index 7. evaluateMF1 also requires the section and a matching work_chunks entry plus concrete content; a mapping alone is not a complete readiness pass. R1's implementation should reuse those actual mapping semantics as it says, leaving malformed/incomplete plan content for GateReadiness. I did not find another selection requirement beyond the detached N4 gap above. Copying or forging valid-looking audit metadata remains possible for any bd metadata writer, as the revised spec explicitly acknowledges; I am not asking for cryptographic authentication or relitigating the anti-footgun threat boundary. The stale-audit finding instead arises from the existing normal writers without forging an audit.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: The final fresh BRIEF's F1 lens still names the successor '129b', contrary to the Round-4 plain-number ruling; O3's lens still describes descendants union metadata.spec_id selection, which R1.1/OQ-9 reject. Its Round-2 history states 95 asks with 91 fixed and 2 refuted, whereas a fresh count of the round-1 coverage table yields 95 rows: 93 FIXED and 2 REFUTED. The suggested git worktree add would register metadata in the source repository despite the read-only requirement; I followed the user's explicit independent-clone instruction instead. The stale AC-count claim reported in my round-3 verdict is now corrected: the BRIEF defers the count to spec.md. These are briefing observations, not additional spec change requests.
